item.title: SciFusion: Physics-Guided Compositional Diffusion for Multimodal 3D Scientific Image Generation
item.description: arXiv:2610.30313v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing 3D generative approaches are typically developed for individual imaging modalities, requiring substantial modality-specific data and limiting their ability to exploit shared structure across scientific imaging domains. We present SciFusion, a multimodal framework for unified 3D scientific image generation built on a latent diffusion backbone, with two key contributions. First, we introduce a compositional conditioning scheme that factorizes each modality into domain, object, and contrast representations. Sharing these factors across related modalities enables knowledge transfer across heterogeneous imaging domains and allows the factors to be recombined at inference time to synthesize unseen domain-object-contrast compositions in a zero-shot manner. Second, we incorporate domain-specific physics-informed objectives: Fourier spectral consistency for MRI, Radon projection consistency for CT, and multislice diffraction consistency for electron microscopy, to encourage generated samples to respect modality-dependent image formation processes. Extensive experiments across 15 medical and scientific imaging modalities demonstrate that SciFusion improves generation fidelity and cross-domain generalization over modality-specific and flattened multimodal conditioning strategies, while enabling zero-shot synthesis of unseen compositions without training on those target compositions. These results demonstrate that compositional, physics-guided conditioning provides a scalable framework for unified 3D scientific image generation, particularly for emerging modalities where large-scale training data are difficult to obtain.
item.dc:creator: Luoxi Wang, Alessio Quercia, Hanno Scharr, Arya Bangun

item.title: A Contrastive Learning Framework for Label-Efficient Gastric Cancer Detection and Intra-Tumour Progression Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2610.30316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gastric Cancer is among the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide. The complexity and variability of histopathological images pose significant challenges for both pathologists and computer-based diagnostics, creating a growing need for machine learning approaches capable of capturing meaningful representations from limited labelled data. Selfsupervised Contrastive Learning (CL) has demonstrated promising results in natural image analysis; however, its application to gastric cancer histopathology remains underexplored. This paper proposes an integrated CL framework built on a ResNet50 encoder trained under the NT-Xent objective, without reliance on ImageNet pre-training, to learn discriminative and staining-invariant representations from H&E-stained tissue patches. The learned embeddings are transferred to a supervised downstream classifier for binary tumour/normal (TUM/NOR) detection, achieving a test accuracy of 83.13%, an AUC-ROC of 0.9087, and an Average Precision of 0.9063 - competitive with recent supervised and weakly-supervised approaches on comparable histopathology benchmarks. Beyond binary diagnosis, the framework applies K-Means clustering to tumour embeddings to identify four geometrically separable pseudo-stage clusters, confirmed by a Random Forest classifier achieving 97% accuracy and a mean Dice coefficient of 0.97, demonstrating the capacity of CL representations to encode progression-relevant morphological variation without stage-level annotations. Grad-CAM explainability is integrated throughout to ensure model transparency. The complete system is deployed via a Streamlit clinical interface. Compared to recent state-of-the-art methods the proposed framework operates with substantially fewer labelled samples while additionally providing unsupervised progression stratification and interpretable outputs, addressing a gap not covered by existing approaches.
item.dc:creator: Aleakhya Pandeti, Pranav M. Pawar, Mithun Mukherjee, Raja Muthalagu

item.title: Unified Projection-Domain Material Decomposition for Energy-Integrating and Photon-Counting CT
item.description: arXiv:2610.30440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Objective: To develop a unified and efficient method for projection-domain material decomposition in spectral computed tomography (CT) that incorporates an arbitrary number of spectral measurements, independent of the acquisition mechanism, without reducing the measurements to two effective energies. Approach: A nested optimization method was developed for two-material basis decomposition from K>=2 spectral measurements. It extends an existing two-measurement univariate method by replacing its polynomial approximation with profile minimization of the Poisson negative log-likelihood, reducing the inversion to two one-dimensional searches that use all measurements without spectral rebinning. The method was evaluated in simulation for energy-integrating (GE Revolution Apex Elite, Siemens SOMATOM Flash) and photon-counting (Siemens NAEOTOM Alpha) CT. Main results: The method recovered line integrals with noiseless iodine errors below 3e-6 g/cm^2 and noise within 3% of the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB). Virtual monoenergetic images (VMIs) agreed, at 70 keV and above, with reference CT numbers and, on all three systems, with vendor VMIs of physical scans (mean absolute error 6-22 HU). For photon counting, four measurements instead of two reduced the iodine CRLB by 19% and image noise by 8-16% at every VMI energy, and lowered the regression error at 70 keV and above. Iteration and tolerance settings changed CT numbers by less than 0.04 HU, and decomposition took 0.34-0.67 s per million rays on an A100 GPU. Significance: The method provides fast, accurate decomposition for any spectral CT acquisition mechanism and number of measurements, so one method can serve every scanner in a virtual imaging trial.
item.dc:creator: Dale Black, Surya Naidu, Hamidreza Khodajou-Chokami, Sabee Molloi

item.title: Equivariant Experience Replay for Continual Learning in Imaging Inverse Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.30460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we propose Equivariant Experience Replay, a new paradigm for achieving continual learning of deep networks for solving ill-posed imaging inverse problems. Inspired by recent advances on unsupervised learning methods such as equivariant imaging/splitting, we find the exploitation of group-symmetry structure is particularly relevant and effective in continual learning setting for ill-posed inversion tasks. We therefore propose this new experience replay scheme, which is tailored for such inverse problems. Our numerical study demonstrates the superiority of our method compared to existing continual learning methods for inverse problems in medical imaging and image processing.
item.dc:creator: Guixian Xu, Jin Zhu, Jinglai Li, Junqi Tang

item.title: CoRE: Relating Fine-Grained Chest X-ray Findings in Anatomical Context
item.description: arXiv:2610.30584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chest X-ray interpretation depends on both the anatomical location of findings and their relationships with other abnormalities. However, relations defined over global finding labels do not explicitly distinguish the same finding across anatomical locations. We propose CoRE(Co-occurrence-guided Region Evidence), a framework that incorporates relationships among findings and anatomical context into fine-grained chest X-ray prediction. It groups anatomical region-finding labels by co-occurrence and uses these groups to guide shared representation learning through visual prompt tuning on a frozen vision transformer. The predictions are supplemented by an anatomically supervised region-evidence stream through region-matched logit residuals. Experiments on MIMIC-CXR with Chest ImaGenome annotations show that CoRE improves region-finding classification over standard and relation-aware prompt-based baselines. Quantitative evaluations on MS-CXR and the Chest ImaGenome gold standard show improved finding localization, supported by qualitative comparisons. CoRE also improves finding-level classification on mapped finding labels in external VinDr-CXR and CheXpert datasets without target-domain adaptation. These results demonstrate the value of jointly modeling finding relationships and anatomical context for fine-grained chest X-ray analysis.
item.dc:creator: Minjun Kim, Jong Hak Moon

item.title: CVP-BAA: Efficiently Adapting Segment Anything Model for Medical Image Segmentation
item.description: arXiv:2610.30672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Various task-specific medical segmentation models have demonstrated strong performance, their heavy reliance on extensive annotations and highly specialized architectures limits their versatility, scalability, and clinical applicability. Recently, adapting vision foundation models, particularly the segment anything model (SAM), has emerged as a promising alternative. However, prevalent parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) strategies, such as prompt tuning and adapter tuning, often lack an explicit mechanism to embed local structural priors into the long-range dependency modeling of vision transformers (ViT), rendering them insufficiently sensitive to fine-grained details. To address these limitations, we introduce CVP-BAA, a novel hybrid PEFT method that improves SAM's sensitivity to domain-specific textures and local details, leading to superior boundary delineation. The proposed CVP-BAA adopts two key ideas. First, it introduces a convolutional visual prompting (CVP) strategy that leverages convolutional features as structural priors, prepending them to the key and value projections within the multi-head self-attention layers of strategically selected ViT blocks. Through a dedicated prompt generation-and-injection module, this mechanism effectively bridges local spatial details with global context semantics. Second, a boundary-aware adapter (BAA) is designed as a parallel branch to the feed-forward network within the same selected blocks. By explicitly computing and amplifying high-frequency components, the BAA enhances feature representations along tissue boundaries and fine-grained lesion structures. Extensive experiments on five benchmarks across three imaging modalities demonstrate that CVP-BAA achieves superior segmentation performance, surpassing existing task-specific models and PEFT-based SAM adaptations in both quantitative metrics and qualitative results.
item.dc:creator: Mei Wang, Minghui Li, Libin Lan

item.title: GWDM: A Guided Wavelet Diffusion Model for Realistic Histopathology Image Generation
item.description: arXiv:2610.30775v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Histopathology images are recognized as a reliable and comprehensive modality for Deep Learning (DL) based diagnosis. However, effectiveness is constrained by limited large-scale annotated datasets, as collecting expert-labeled medical data is costly and time-intensive. Recent advances in generative models, particularly diffusion models, demonstrate strong capabilities in synthesizing medically relevant content for dataset augmentation. Existing generative frameworks treat histopathology patches as generic natural images, failing to enforce biological constraints such as histomorphological structures and heterogeneous staining patterns essential for valid synthesis. We propose a guided wavelet diffusion model (GWDM) framework that captures image details at multiple scales using wavelets and leverages controllable conditioning based on domain-specific histopathological features (e.g., tissue patterns and color variations). We further formulate a histomorphological guidance loss applied to real and generated patches. A loss ramping strategy gradually introduces these constraints during training, ensuring stable optimization and robust modeling of tissue architecture. GWDM was evaluated on three benchmark datasets (BCSS, MoNuSeg, and PAIP2019), consistently outperforming state-of-the-art generative methods. Ablation studies confirmed that domain-guided conditioning, perceptual loss, and structural similarity loss each contribute meaningfully to synthesis quality. Downstream nuclei and tissue segmentation experiments further validated the clinical utility of GWDM-generated images, demonstrating consistent performance improvements when synthetic data augments real training sets. This work shows that domain-specific conditioning and dual-loss optimization generate realistic histopathology patches, reducing data scarcity and improving clinical downstream segmentation performance.
item.dc:creator: Abdullah, Tao Huang, Ickjai Lee, Lei Bi, Euijoon Ahn

item.title: H-2DGS: Height-Field Gaussian Splatting for Sharp and Deformable Neurosurgical Surface Reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2610.30910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neurosurgical navigation commonly presents magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) as 2D slices, making it difficult to relate the anatomy in those slices to the cortical surface observed through the surgical microscope. We seek a common 3D visualization that combines a photorealistic reconstruction of the exposed cortex during tumor surgery with whole-brain MRI context and diffusion tractography pathways. This requires the reconstructed cortex to form a clear boundary around the brain anatomy rather than a diffuse volume that obscures internal structures. Conventional 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) can reproduce observed views but, under limited surgical view coverage, may distribute opacity through a thick and geometrically ambiguous band. We introduce height-field 2D Gaussian Splatting (H-2DGS), a three-stage pipeline that concentrates a robust 3DGS reconstruction, fuses its depth into a shared truncated signed distance field (TSDF) surface, and represents that surface with curved, surface-oriented Gaussian primitives. Separate height, color, and opacity bases provide local geometry and appearance, while a neighbor-transition objective coordinates overlapping patches. The explicit surface further supports postoperative alignment: MRI-derived depth deforms the reconstruction, and tracked-color supervision with alternating optimization preserves its appearance. Across five real neurosurgical cases, H-2DGS gives low multi-view depth inconsistency, a compact 7.97MB representation, and interactive rendering at 29--42ms per frame. The resulting sharp, deformable surface integrates clearly with tractography and MRI anatomy, including a postoperative resection cavity.
item.dc:creator: Zhang Zichuan, Bart Brouwers, Rembrandt Bakker, Maud Landers, Geert-Jan Rutten, Maxime Chamberland

item.title: Vision Transformers for Estimating Irradiance Using Data Scarce Sky Images
item.description: arXiv:2610.30940v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate estimation of diffuse horizontal irradiance (DHI) is critical for optimising photovoltaic system performance and energy forecasting yet remains challenging in regions lacking comprehensive ground-based instrumentation. Recent advancements using Vision Transformers (ViTs) trained on extensive sky image datasets have shown promise in replacing costly irradiance measurement equipment, but the scarcity of long-term, high-quality sky imagery significantly restricts practical implementation. Addressing this critical gap, this study proposes a novel dual-framework approach designed for data-scarce scenarios. First, calculated atmospheric parameters, including extraterrestrial irradiance and cyclic time encodings, are integrated to represent sky conditions without utilising any instrumentation. Next, a sequential pipeline initially predicts synthetic global horizontal irradiance (GHI) and uses it as a feature, to refine DHI estimation. Finally, a dual-parallel architecture simultaneously processes raw and overlay-enhanced fisheye sky images. Overlays are generated through unsupervised, physics-informed cloud segmentation to highlight dynamic sky features. Empirical validation is performed using data from the Chilbolton Observatory, chosen for its temperate climate and frequent cloud variability. To simulate data-scarce conditions, models are trained on a single month (e.g., January) and evaluated across a temporally disjoint, full-year test set. Under this setup, the sequential and dual-parallel frameworks achieve RMSE values within 2-3 W/m^2 and 1-6 W/m^2, respectively, of a state-of-the-art ViT trained on the complete dataset. By combining physics-informed modelling with unsupervised segmentation, the proposed method provides a scalable and cost-effective solution for DHI estimation, advancing solar resource assessment in data-constrained environments.
item.dc:creator: David Hamlyn, Sunny Chaudhary, Tasmiat Rahman

item.title: GateFormer: Forecast-Space Decomposition for Intra-Hour Solar Irradiance Prediction from Sky Images
item.description: arXiv:2610.30942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sub-hourly dispatch, balancing, and storage control increasingly depend on forecasts that anticipate rapid variability in solar generation. Accurate sky-image-based irradiance forecasting requires a combination of visual cloud dynamics with recent irradiance state while adapting to different short-term irradiance-change regimes. To address this, we introduce GateFormer, a GHI-conditioned dual-decoder ViT for intra-hour global horizontal irradiance (GHI) forecasting through forecast-space decomposition. GateFormer embeds observed GHI into the visual token stream, allowing interaction with sky-image patch features through self-attention. From this shared representation, a Trajectory Head predicts future GHI sequence, while a Delta Head predicts final-horizon change from the latest observed GHI. The two final-horizon forecasts are adaptively weighted in prediction space, with magnitude- and direction-supervision targeting the remaining error. On the NREL-TSI benchmark, GateFormer attains 125.01 W/m^2 RMSE at +30 min, improving over a state-of-the-art transformer baseline by 9.6% under paired-timestamp evaluation. Across NREL-TSI, Chilbolton, and SIRTA, GateFormer achieves the lowest final-horizon RMSE among the evaluated baselines, with forecast skill of 22.97-28.86% relative to smart persistence. Component ablations show adaptive weighting outperforms both individual decoders and fixed averaging, distinguishing GateFormer from conventional forecast combination, while the supervised correction further reduces RMSE by 1.68 W/m^2 and MAE by 4.86 W/m^2. Ramp-regime diagnostics show larger gains during operationally important positive ramps, reducing RMSE by 26.27 W/m^2. These results identify forecast-space decomposition as an alternative forecasting formulation, with potential relevance to other multimodal short-horizon forecasting tasks and deployment using only sky images and measured GHI.
item.dc:creator: David Hamlyn, Sunny Chaudhary, Jonathon Hare, Tasmiat Rahman

item.title: Bound-Conditioned Latent Inference for Progressive Image Compression
item.description: arXiv:2610.30966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Progressive image compression reconstructs images from prefixes of a single bitstream and therefore involves sequential latent inference under partial observations. Existing trit-plane codecs mainly treat decoded trits as discrete symbols for probability prediction, without fully exploiting their role as interval constraints on the underlying continuous latents. We propose bound-conditioned latent inference (BLI), a framework that reformulates progressive trit-plane coding as sequential latent inference under shrinking interval constraints. At each coding step, the trits decoded so far define lower and upper bounds for each latent element. BLI uses the center and width of these bounds, together with hyperprior information shared by the encoder and decoder, to jointly refine the Gaussian parameters $(\mu,\sigma)$ for entropy modeling and the latent estimate $\hat{y}$ for reconstruction. As additional trits are decoded, the feasible intervals shrink monotonically, yielding tighter constraints for the next inference step and enabling flexible in-plane refinement schedules. Experiments on Kodak, CLIC, and JPEG-AI show that BLI achieves state-of-the-art rate-distortion performance among progressive image codecs, reducing BD-rate by $17.78\%$ over DPICT and by $7.96\%$ over CTC on Kodak, while replacing CTC's plane-specific predictors with a shared model that uses about $5.3\times$ fewer parameters and achieves lower latency than CTC.
item.dc:creator: Jaeseok Jang, Seungmin Jeon, Kwang Pyo Choi, Chang-Su Kim

item.title: QICOM: Open-Source Software for Reproducible Image Quality Evaluation, Blinded Assessment, and Radiomic Comparison
item.description: arXiv:2610.31218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: QICOM (Quality Image COMparator) is open-source software for quantitative image comparison, paired radiomics, and blinded assessment. It saves processing settings, image identities, measurements, and response mappings so a comparison can be reopened and recalculated. We evaluate reference agreement, responses to controlled perturbations, and recovery of saved analyses. Synthetic experiments cover 37 quantitative descriptors using independentnumerical references and separate upstream integration comparisons. The QICOM/MIRP backend meets the reference tolerances for all 482 numeric IBSI 1 digital-phantom entries and all 1,622 entries across configurations A-E of the public CT reference case; these comprise 1,804 feature/aggregation comparisons and 300 preprocessing diagnostics. Restricting masked SSIM and HFEN to complete kernel support removes the observed dependence on excluded pixels. In a synthetic filtering example, stronger smoothing increases SSIM while worsening MSE and HFEN relative to milder smoothing and changing GLCM contrast more strongly. Reopened radiomics projects reproduce all 43 feature pairs per comparison, and two blinded deliveries return four correctly mapped scripted responses. These experiments document the calculations and data transfers linking the three workflows.
item.dc:creator: Fabio Mattiussi, Switinder Ghotra

item.title: Self-Supervised Multibeam Sonar Restoration via Coherent Forward Modeling
item.description: arXiv:2610.31490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multibeam imaging sonar produces intensity images degraded by coherent speckle and system-induced blur, while clean reflectivity targets are rarely available. Existing despeckling methods often rely on simplified intensity-domain noise models, synthetic clean targets, or blind-spot self-supervision, and typically do not jointly model deblurring and speckle suppression. We propose a physics-consistent self-supervised framework for joint despeckling and deblurring of multibeam imaging sonar. A stochastic coherent image-formation model yields a conditional-mean forward operator that relates latent scene reflectivity to expected intensity through the squared magnitude of the system point spread function. We then use registered multi-frame sonar sequences to train without clean ground truth images, showing that, under an idealized inter-frame conditional-mean condition, the expected paired loss equals the corresponding forward-prediction loss up to a network-independent constant. To stabilize the ill-conditioned inverse problem, we further adapt robust equivariant imaging using stochastic coherent simulation and introduce a paired forward prediction error metric for ground-truth-free evaluation. Experiments on two real multibeam sonar datasets demonstrate a favourable balance between forward-prediction agreement, homogeneous-region speckle suppression, and preservation of visible structural boundaries compared with representative baselines.
item.dc:creator: Zixin Wang, James Hopgood, Mike Davies

item.title: AVAtt: A Free-Viewing Eye-Tracking Dataset and Benchmark for Visual Attention on Paintings
item.description:
arXiv:2610.30481v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Saliency and scanpath models are developed almost exclusively on natural photographs, yet paintings are composed by artists to guide the viewer's eye and differ from photographs in texture, colour and abstraction. We introduce \avatt, a free-viewing eye-tracking dataset on 
Images{} paintings spanning sixteen art movements and five centuries, with 
Scanpaths{} scanpaths and 
Fixations{} fixations from 
Participants{} participants (\spPerImageMin--\spPerImageMax{} observers per painting). For every painting we release individual scanpaths with fixation timing and eye--screen distance, fixation maps, saliency maps smoothed at one degree of visual angle, temporal saliency videos and rich art metadata. We benchmark classic and deep saliency models against human agreement, revealing substantial headroom for art-aware models, and rank 44 scanpath-similarity measures, including a new language-free family of image-encoder metrics built on ten CNN, ViT and self-supervised encoders. With controls that remove viewing biases, we show that faces are fixated  aceEnrich$	imes$ more than expected and within half a second, that local structure draws the eye, that composition rules fitted from image content predict where people look, and that art style shapes how much viewers agree. Dataset, code and a Python package are available at: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Amine-CV/AVAtt.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Amine Kerkouri, Marouane Tliba, Aladine Chetouani, Alessandro Bruno

item.title: Beyond MSE: Rician Likelihood Denoising for Self-Supervised Cardiac $T2$ and $T1\rho$ MRI
item.description: arXiv:2609.31777v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging involves an inherent trade-off among spatial resolution, acquisition time, and noise. This trade-off contributes to long scan times and high cost. Deep learning has improved image denoising, but cardiac MRI remains difficult because high-resolution, rapid acquisitions generally lack corresponding low-noise ground truth. Self-supervised denoising offers a potential solution by learning from noisy image pairs or even single noisy acquisitions. However, we show that Noise2Void-style blind-spot denoising, which uses a mean squared error (MSE) loss and assumes zero-mean, independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) noise, is poorly suited to MR magnitude images. When applied to short-axis $T2$-weighted and $T1\rho$-weighted cardiac MRI with synthetic Rician noise, it produces biased denoised images and biased parametric maps of $T2$ and $T1\rho$. To address this limitation, we formulate self-supervised denoising as maximum likelihood estimation under a known Rician noise model. This yields unbiased denoisers that are competitive with supervised baselines.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas A. Jacobs, Jason Mendes, Ravi Ranjan, Edward DiBella, Shireen Elhabian

item.title: A Simple yet Effective Framework for Pre-treatment and Post-treatment Glioma Segmentation Using Multimodal MRI
item.description: arXiv:2610.01060v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurate glioma segmentation across pre- and post-treatment MRI remains challenging because treatment alters both image appearance and the target regions. In particular, the resection cavity (RC) is defined only for post-treatment cases, complicating joint learning from pooled data. We present RC-aware nnU-Netv2, a simple yet effective glioma segmentation framework that combines lesion- and boundary-aware single-cohort training, an RC-aware joint learning objective, and treatment-status-guided model routing at inference. During pooled training, the joint objective applies both standard and boundary-weighted binary cross-entropy to all four region channels, while employing Dice supervision for channels with non-empty targets and a controlled false-positive penalty for channels with empty targets across the mini-batch. This design explicitly accommodates the absence of RC in pre-treatment cases. Our approach uses only the standard nnU-Netv2 data augmentation and a single specialized model per case, without additional synthetic tumor generation or multi-model ensembling. RC-aware nnU-Netv2 ranked second in the BraTS 2025 Lighthouse Challenge Task 1 (BraTS-GLI 2025), with segmentation performance comparable to that of the first-place method, which relied on on-the-fly GliGAN-based synthetic tumor augmentation and multi-model ensembling. On the official blind test set, our method achieved mean lesion-wise Dice scores of 0.7878, 0.8709, 0.7923, and 0.8715 and mean NSD@1.0 scores of 0.8309, 0.8712, 0.7980, and 0.8336 for enhancing tumor, RC, tumor core, and whole tumor, respectively. In paired post-treatment analysis, the RC-aware joint model improved mean lesion-wise Dice by 0.042 (95% CI: [0.028, 0.057]) and mean NSD@1.0 by 0.043 (95% CI: [0.028, 0.059]) compared with the joint baseline.
item.dc:creator: Lin Qu, Ziqi Chen, Anqi Wu, Jinyao Shen, Hai Shu

item.title: Deficit-Driven Stratified Acquisition for Building STRATA-S12: An Open SAR-Optical Corpus for Self-Supervised Learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.17680v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Building a co-registered SAR-optical corpus for self-supervised Earth Observation is above all an acquisition problem, yet the main multi-modal datasets are collected opportunistically, with no per-stratum quota control, so the regions and seasons that cloud cover hits hardest end up under-sampled. We present Deficit-Driven Stratified Acquisition (DDSA), an algorithm that casts the construction of a Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 corpus as a constrained maximum-coverage problem over a land-cover-driven, hemisphere-corrected (class x season x region) stratification of target countries on all six inhabited continents, and solves it online: acquisition is ordered by marginal gain against a per-stratum deficit that the quality gates and a visual review of every accepted pair keep updating during the run. Three results follow from measuring the algorithm on its own product. First, stratum balance is a property of the deficit-driven ordering rather than of run length: replayed over all 2,928,370 real acquisition attempts, failures included, it populates all 192 strata within 0.05% of the attempts, against 4.03% for uniform round-robin effort and 20.5% for a random order. Second, whether a rejected attempt can be recovered is better predicted by how long its cause persists than by the type of defect: cloud rejections are recovered at eta = 18.8% against 41.4% for nodata, consistent with clouds persisting through a season. Third, the repair loop supplies 39.5% of the released pairs at no measurable quality cost, with 89.8% surviving manual review, but it adds yield rather than balance. The quality guarantee has a price: 2,928,370 acquisition attempts produced 740,746 released pairs. We release the corpus, STRATA-S12, with per-pair metadata sidecars aligned with the STAC and PDS4 standards and the FAIR principles, and a pre-registered linear probe confirms it is fit for self-supervised pre-training.
item.dc:creator: Christian Sanchez-Leon, Dongming Chen, Dongqi Wang
